title: finding(ci): `.github/labeler.yml` has no rule matching `content/**`, so a PR touching only the 203-file published docs tree draws ZERO labels — and `sync-labels: true` removes one applied by hand
body:
`.github/labeler.yml` has **no rule matching `content/**`**, so a pull request touching only the
published documentation tree draws **zero** labels. The `documentation` rule covers `docs/**/*`,
`*.md` and `packages/**/README.md` — the 25-file internal tree, ⛔ not the 203-file published one.
And because the workflow runs with `sync-labels: true`, a label applied by hand is **removed** on the
next synchronize.

Measured by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat at 2026-09-19T11:16Z, with PR objectui#10011 as the live probe.

## The probe, and its control

| reading <sub>all rows read 2026-09-19T11:16Z</sub> | value |
|:--|:--|
| PR objectui#10011 — touches `content/docs/guide/user-state-persistence.md` only | created 2026-09-19T11:10:25Z |
| workflow `Auto Label PRs`, run `35439380882` | ran 2026-09-19T11:10:35Z, conclusion **success** |
| labels on that PR afterwards | **(none)** |
| **CONTROL** — the same workflow on package PRs | objectui#10009 → `package: react, tests`; objectui#10008 → `plugin, tests` |

⇒ the workflow ran, succeeded, and assigned nothing. The control is what makes that a reading rather
than a broken run.

## The rule, and the two trees

`.github/labeler.yml:108`-`:113`:

```yaml
'documentation':
  - changed-files:
    - any-glob-to-any-file:
      - 'docs/**/*'
      - '*.md'
      - 'packages/**/README.md'
```

⛔ Nothing in that file mentions `content/` at all — `git grep 'content/' -- .github/labeler.yml`
returns **zero**, and the same command returns matches for other prefixes in the same file, so the
zero is a reading.

| tracked files <sub>read 2026-09-19T11:16Z</sub> | count |
|:--|--:|
| `content/docs` — the published docs site | **203** |
| `docs/` — the internal tree the rule covers | **25** |

⇒ the label covers the smaller tree and misses the one users read.

## ⭐ The second half is worse than the gap

`.github/workflows/labeler.yml:73` runs `actions/labeler@v7` and `:77` sets **`sync-labels: true`**.
`documentation` IS a config-defined label, so the labeler owns it wholesale: the label a human or a
seat applies by hand to a `content/**`-only PR is **removed on the next synchronize**. On
objectui#10011 the dev applied it by hand after seeing the empty set; that label is living on
borrowed time.

⚠️ Related but ⛔ not a duplicate: objectstack#19179 records the general `sync-labels: true` hazard —
that ANY hand-applied PR label is wiped. This card is the narrower, concrete instance plus the
missing-rule half, which that card does not carry.

## Why it matters, in the file's own words

`.github/labeler.yml`'s own header states the harm for packages: 「a package with no entry here draws
no label, so its PRs are invisible to any sweep keyed on `package: *`」. The same sentence applies to
the docs tree verbatim — ⭐ except that packages have a coverage pin
(`scripts/__tests__/labeler-package-coverage.test.ts`, which runs green) and the docs tree has
**none**. ⇒ the gap is unfalsifiable today: nothing fails when a tree is missing from that file.

## Two directions, ⛔ neither chosen here

1. **Add the rule** — glob `content/**/*` into `documentation` (or mint a separate label if the two
   trees want distinguishing). Smallest change; leaves the class unfalsifiable for the next tree.
2. **Extend the coverage pin to trees, not just packages.** `labeler-package-coverage.test.ts`
   already proves the shape works; a sibling asserting that every tracked top-level content tree is
   matched by at least one rule would have caught this and will catch the next one. ⚠️ Needs a
   decision about which trees are in the population, which is why it is offered rather than taken.

Dedupe words: `labeler content/docs no rule` · `documentation label sync-labels removed` ·
`labeler-package-coverage docs tree` · `Auto Label PRs zero labels` · `objectui#7746 labeler`
